analysis:
Examined the docs/reference/protocol-messages.md excerpts, the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer bump and the EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift patch.

The doc changes only update the date and describe freshness semantics for performance observations: sample_age_ms now follows the newest observation. They add no wire or auth changes and no new fields.

In EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift, Rate.observe now takes a keepsNewest flag and sets at = max(at, now) when it is on. The flag defaults to DeadlineAdmissionFixes.enabled. It adds coversObservation and observationAge helpers. This only affects capacity and performance-rate freshness telemetry used for deadline admission and routing. It touches no keys, ciphertext, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-053) or prefix-cache storage (T-041). The app-reported rate evidence stays advisory and is bounded by the coordinator's own validation. The doc states these samples cannot certify a profile or change billing.

A possible concern is that a provider could keep stale rates looking fresh. The provider is already adversarial and self-reports these values, and a late completed observation cannot make the timestamp go backwards. The max() clamp could in theory hold a timestamp ahead of now. wire() clamps the age with max(0, ...), so the age cannot go negative. The restart/EWMA gap logic still uses now - at, which can be negative after max(); the effect is only a smoothing difference.

The submodule bump (libs/mlx-swift-lm, 19634dd to 4b8a1bb) is opaque: only the commit hashes are visible and the diff is not supplied. I cannot assess its security impact. This is a coverage limit, so I recommend someone review the submodule diff, especially anything touching KV cache, memory or prefix-cache behavior (T-041, T-028, TB-007). The remainder of the Swift file beyond the patch excerpt was truncated, and callers of the new coversObservation/observationAge were not supplied.
